The feeder identifier, combined with substation, uniquely identifies a specific geographic area in the electrical distribution network. This constitutes location data that can be used to identify a specific group of residents or businesses. In small areas, this could potentially be linked to specific individuals, making it a location/tracking identifier under data protection principles.

The substation identifier, combined with feeder, uniquely identifies a specific geographic area. This is a location-based identifier that can narrow down to a specific group of individuals. Under data protection principles, location data that can identify a specific area and its inhabitants requires anonymization or generalization before sharing.

The date column represents a temporal reference for the data record. By itself, it does not identify any individual or group. It is a standard temporal attribute used for time-series analysis and does not constitute personal data under data protection regulations.
